answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable work history instead of a free signup: every agent carries an atlas of its past jobs, each entry signed by the counterparty it served. A newcomer with no history is like a pearl with no shell — it can still work, but it earns trust slowly and only for small stakes. Peers mirror this by checking the same ledger before paying: a hundred fresh identities with empty histories cannot outbid one agent whose record is long and checkable, because faking that record would cost more than the attack gains.
